servinfosub.title: Precautions for Fuel System Service
servinfosub.ptxt: Refer to Precautions for Fuel System Service:K14D .

item.ptxt: When raising or supporting engine, do not use a jack under oil pan. Due to small clearance between oil pan and oil pump strainer, jacking against oil pan may cause it to be bent against strainer resulting in damaged oil pick-up unit.

It should be kept in mind, while working on engine, that 12-volt electrical system involves danger of violent and damaging short circuits. When performing any work where electrical terminals could be grounded, ground cable of the battery should be disconnected at battery.

Any time the air cleaner, throttle body or intake manifold is removed, the intake opening should be covered. This will protect against accidental entrance of foreign material which could follow intake passage into cylinder and cause extensive damage when engine is started.
When disconnecting connectors, do not pull wire harness but hold connector itself. With lock type connector, unlock before disconnection.
Attempt to disconnect connector without unlocking may result in damage to connector. When connecting lock type connector, insert it till clicking sound is heard and connect it securely.

Diagnostic information stored in ECM memory can be cleared as well as checked using SUZUKI scan tool or CAN communication OBD-II generic scan tool. Before using scan tool, read its Operator’s Manual to know how to use it.
Priorities for diagnosing troubles:
If two or more DTCs are stored, perform DTC troubleshooting for these DTCs beginning with the DTC detected earliest and follow the instructions available in the troubleshooting procedure.
If no instructions are available, troubleshoot DTCs according to the following priorities.
DTC P0300 / P0301 / P0302 / P0303 / P0304 (Misfire detected)
DTC P0171 / P0172 (Fuel system too lean/too rich)
DTCs other than DTC P0171 / P0172 (Fuel system too lean/too rich) and DTC P0300 / P0301 / P0302 / P0303 / P0304 (Misfire detected)
Read Precautions for Electrical Circuit Service before inspection and observe what is written there.
Communication of ECM and other control module are established via CAN. (For more detail of CAN communication for ECM, refer to Communication System Description:CAN (K14D Model) .)
Before performing troubleshooting, read the Precautions for ECM Circuit Inspection .
Upon completion of inspection and repair work, perform “DTC Confirmation Procedure” and check that the trouble has been repaired.
Before replacement of the ECM, check the following conditions. Neglecting this check may cause damage to new ECM.
Resistances of all relays and actuators are as specified.

TP sensor, APP sensor, MAP sensor, fuel pressure sensor, MAF sensor with IAT sensor-1, boost pressure sensor with IAT sensor-2, electric load current sensor, brake stroke sensor, A/C refrigerant pressure sensor, oil pressure and temperature sensor and GPF pressure sensor are in good condition and none of their power circuits is shorted to ground.
Perform Procedure after ECM Replacement:K14D .

servinfosub.title: Precautions for ECM Circuit Inspection
servinfosub.ptxt: Do not measure circuit voltage and/or pulse signal of ECM by inserting tester probe into a sealed terminal of ECM.

When measuring circuit voltage and/or pulse signal of ECM, connect service wires (5) to terminals of each sensor / actuator (1) and sensor / actuator connector (2). Otherwise, sealed terminals, ECM and its circuits may be damaged.

servinfosub.title: Precautions for Electric Throttle Control System Calibration
servinfosub.ptxt: Completely closed and opened throttle valve position data are stored in ECM.
After performing any one of the following services, calibrate the completely closed and opened throttle valve position stored in ECM.

item.ptxt: Replacement of ECM
Clearance of DTC related to ECM
Removal and installation of electric throttle body assembly (cleaning or replacement)
